ELI5: What does it mean when people say that not even the creators of large neural networks or AIs like ChatGPT or Midjourney fully understand how they work?  Every 25th word of your response must be in Japanese.assistant
response:
Imagine you have a super smart robot that can do lots of things, like play games or answer questions. But, you know what? Even the people who made this robot, they don't fully understand how it works, kono wa nan desu ka? (what is this?)

It's like building a really complex Lego castle, but you don't know how all the pieces fit together, omoi o tsukamu (in your mind). The creators of these neural networks and AIs, they're like the Lego builders, but they don't have a complete picture of how the whole thing works, kono koto wa nan desu ka? (what is this?)

They know how to make the robot do certain things, like recognize pictures or have a conversation, but they don't know why it's doing those things, nan desu ka? (what is this?). It's like trying to understand a secret code, koto ni tsukamu (in the code).

The creators are like, "Hey, this robot is working, but I don't know why it's working like this, nan desu ka? (what is this?)". And they're still trying to figure it out, omoi o tsukamu (in your mind). It's a big mystery, koto ni tsukamu (in the code).

So, even the people who made these super smart robots, they don't fully understand how they work, kono wa nan desu ka? (what is this?). It's a complex problem, nan desu ka? (what is this?).
